# qwen21-nsfw-pose [![Package checks](https://github.com/Arekejoker/qwen21-nsfw-pose-skill/actions/workflows/validate.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/Arekejoker/qwen21-nsfw-pose-skill/actions/workflows/validate.yml) **Qwen-Image 2.1 本地 NSFW / 姿势出图完整配方** — 作者级提示词结构 + NSFW LoRA + 136 个 3D 姿势库 + VNCCS 人偶精确姿势控制。 基于 ComfyUI + `qwen_image_2.1_int8_convrot` 底模（与 Civitai 作者同款底模），复刻并验证过 Civitai 作者样图（2026-10-12）。 - 适用：Claude Code / Codex / Cursor / OpenClaw（agent 技能）+ 人类手动使用 - 内容：可跟跑的作者案例、强制配方、姿势大胆度阶梯（L0–L3）、完整依赖与安装指南 **演示**（3D 人偶调姿势 → 一键生成 → 成品，Route ④）： --- ## 效果展示 ### 本配方输出：同一海边场景的三级对照（L0 → L1 → L2） | L0 · 全着装，无 LoRA（提示词即全部） | L1 · 湿身泳装 + LoRA@1.0 | L2 · 极低机位 + 湿身蹲姿 + LoRA@1.0 | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | 三张图同场景递进：L0 只有提示词；L1 加 LoRA + 显式皮肤/水珠描写；L2 再加低机位与开合姿态。**LoRA 负责质感，提示词负责信息密度，机位负责大胆度。** ### NSFW 效果（⚠️ 以下图片包含裸露内容）

👇 点击上方卡片展开作者原图（含裸露内容 · 18+，再点收起） **作者原图**（Civitai showcase，本配方复刻的目标）： | 作者 · 淋浴（tawsLoRa） | 作者 · 按摩（tawsLoRa） | 作者 · 自拍（TheseAlpacas） | | --- | --- | --- | | | | |
用 §「快速开始」的命令可复刻淋浴那张（复刻输出已验证与作者原图同场景同构图，见 `downloads/samples/phase5_meta.json` 与本文快速开始一节）。 ### 3D 人偶精确姿势（Route ④，136 姿势库） 默认人物图 `references/src_standing.png`；姿势 = 骨骼旋转 JSON（MakeHuman 网格 + three.js 渲染）， 换姿势且保身份。姿势库来源：HuggingFace 4 个公开仓库（`Totemistyk/General_Poses`、 `Totemistyk/Ballet_PoseStudio`、`MIUProject/VNCCS_PoseLibrary_Main`、 `MIUProject/MySuperPoseRepo`）+ 55 个手工精选，共 **136 个**。 --- ## 快速开始（作者案例跟跑） 前置安装见 [install/setup.md](install/setup.md)。装好后先跑一次自检（只读，不改动任何东西）： ```bash python3 scripts/doctor.py ``` 它逐项检查 ComfyUI 连通性、底模/LoRA、VNCCS 节点、姿势库、浏览器后端，并给出缺失项的修复指引。 全绿后一条命令复刻作者淋浴样图（~5 分钟）： ```bash python3 scripts/qwen_pose_test.py \ --mode t2i --name author_case_shower \ --prompt "$(cat prompts/taws_v13_shower.txt)" \ --seed 80964 \ --steps 50 --cfg 2.5 --sampler er_sde --scheduler beta \ --width 1152 --height 1728 \ --lora "qwen2_1-femaledVaginus-nsfw-v1_3-fine_L22-31.safetensors" \ --lora-strength 1.0 \ --out outputs/author_case/shower.png ``` 对比对象：`downloads/samples/taws_v13_shower_author.jpg`。 完整元数据（提示词/参数/seed/完整工作流）：`downloads/samples/phase5_meta.json`。 ### 硬件要求（参考） 底模为 Qwen-Image 2.1 int8 套件，模型文件合计约 16GB（diffusion 6.8GB / text encoder 8.7GB / VAE 0.6GB），LoRA 各自 ≤608MB。 - **最低**：NVIDIA 12GB 显存 + 32GB 内存——能跑，ComfyUI 会自动把部分模型卸载到内存，出图慢一些 - **推荐**：24GB 显存（3090/4090 级）+ 32–64GB 内存——模型基本常驻，体验最顺 - **8GB 显存**：建议用 GGUF 量化版（社区实测 12–16GB 显存可跑 Q4；8GB 靠 offload 会明显更慢） - 纯 CPU 不推荐（单张图耗时过长） - 硬盘预留 ~40GB；CPU 无特殊要求（现代 x86_64/ARM 均可）；Linux 最省事，Windows 建议 WSL2；Mac（Apple Silicon）见下方单独小节 - 路线④额外需要一个可连接的桌面浏览器（Playwright/CDP，见 `install/setup.md`） 本仓库案例图与实测数据来自统一内存设备（DGX Spark）：1024×1024、40 步约 32 秒/张，峰值增量约 7–10GB。 ### macOS（Apple Silicon） - 适用 M 系芯片（M1 及以上）；Intel Mac 不建议 - **模型选择看统一内存**：≥32GB 直接用本仓库原版 int8 套件（ComfyUI + MPS）；16–32GB 建议改用 GGUF 量化版（搭配 ComfyUI-GGUF；社区实测 Q8 更快、Q4 更省内存） - **速度预期：分钟级/张**——社区报告：M5 Pro 48GB 跑 int8 约 144 秒/1024；M1 Max 64GB 约 7–10 分钟/张（加缓存优化节点如 Comfyui-Spectrum-Qwen2.1 可提速 2–3 倍）。对比本仓库 DGX Spark 实测 32 秒/张，仅供参考 - 已知坑：编辑模式在 MPS 上偶发 VAE 编码异常，可用 ComfyUI 的 `--cpu-vae` 绕过（ComfyUI issue #16433，已有修复讨论）；内存紧张时建议单张生成、关闭其他大内存应用 - 路线兼容：①②③ 脚本在 macOS 可直接运行（纯 Python 标准库、POSIX 兼容）；④ 需 `playwright install chromium`（macOS 版），`install/setup.md` 中的 AppArmor 提示不适用 - ⚠️ 以上 Mac 数据来自社区报告，维护者没有 Mac 硬件、未经实测；如果你在 Mac 上跑通或遇到问题，欢迎开 issue 反馈，我们会持续更新本说明 ## 四条路线 | 需求 | 路线 | 命令 | | --- | --- | --- | | 新 NSFW/性感图（文字出图） | ① T2I + NSFW LoRA（必开） | `scripts/qwen_pose_test.py --mode t2i` | | 已有角色图换姿势（保脸/保服装） | ② Edit | `scripts/qwen_pose_test.py --mode edit` | | 已有 3D 人偶姿势渲染图，脚本换姿势（不开浏览器） | ③ 脚本姿势迁移（人偶参考 + VNCCS LoRA） | `scripts/run_pose_transfer.py --char <角色图> --pose-ref <人偶渲染图> --out <出图.png>` | | 指定 3D 姿势库里的精确姿势 | ④ VNCCS PoseStudio | `scripts/run_vnccs_ui.py --pose [--prompt "<场景>"]` | 路线③的人偶参考图可由路线④的运行自动保存（输出目录里的 `doll_*.png`），或任何 3D 姿态渲染图。 不要用照片/插画当姿势参考——模型会把参考人物拼进画面，或直接重画参考人物；请使用无身份特征的 3D 人偶渲染图（路线③/④）。 姿势怎么选（大胆度阶梯 L0–L3、用户要求→姿势族映射表）：见 `SKILL.md` §4，或 `scripts/run_vnccs_ui.py --list-poses` 列出全部 136 个姿势。 ## 配方要点（摘要） - `er_sde` + `beta`，CFG 2.5，50 步，1152×1728 竖版 - **NSFW LoRA 永远开**（默认 `femaledVaginus v1.3b` @ 1.0） - 提示词必须按作者结构写满 7 要素、300–1500 字符、含 LoRA 触发词 - 弱化配方（无 LoRA/短提示词/减步数）前必须告知用户代价，不许默默减弱 完整规则与证据：`SKILL.md`。 ## 目录结构 ``` ├── SKILL.md # agent 技能（完整规则） ├── install/setup.md # 安装指南（模型/LoRA/节点/姿势库） ├── scripts/ # doctor.py 自检、出图/自定义姿势脚本、浏览器 fallback、media_lock.py、validate_package.py ├── workflows/ # qwen21_t2i.json / qwen21_edit.json / VNCCS_PoseStudio_QI2.1.json ├── prompts/ # 3 篇作者原提示词 + 参数 ├── references/ # 效果展示图（L0/L1/L2 海边对照）+ 默认人物图 ├── downloads/samples/ # 作者原图 + 作者元数据 + 原始工作流 JSON └── pose_library/ # 55 个手工精选姿势（安装时拷入 ComfyUI） ``` ## 说明 - 本仓库原创代码与文档（`scripts/`、`workflows/`、`prompts/`、`SKILL.md`、README 等）采用 [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE) - 第三方素材不在 Apache-2.0 覆盖范围内，权利归各自原作者：`downloads/samples/` 作者原图（Civitai 作者）、`pose_library/` 社区姿势与预览（MIUProject / Totemistyk，其中 Ballet 仓库为 MIT）、模型与 LoRA（HF `Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1`、Civitai 2986844 / 2958918 / 2988215、RunningHubAI、MIUProject 等） - NSFW 示例图仅供配方演示；仓库为公开仓库，介意图片的先收藏后阅读 ## 致谢 本仓库的姿势控制能力（路线③④）与 136 姿势库基于 [AHEKOT](https://github.com/AHEKOT/ComfyUI_VNCCS_Utils)（VNCCS_Utils）、[Totemistyk](https://huggingface.co/Totemistyk)、[MIUProject](https://huggingface.co/MIUProject) 的开源工作；底模与 LoRA 来自 Qwen / Comfy-Org、RunningHubAI 及 Civitai 的 tawsLoRa、TheseAlpacas、posture-v3。感谢所有作者。

items.title: feder-cr/git-ai
items.readme:
Git designed for AI agents.

Anthropic built **Scion**, a faster version control system for coding agents, and described it in [Redesigning source control](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/redesigning-source-control): a server-centric system built for hundreds of agents that read, write and land code at the same time. Scion is internal to Anthropic and is not available to the public. So I built **gitai**: an open-source version of that design that anyone can run, and that the community can improve and maintain together. MIT licensed. Vendor neutral: the server never calls a language model, and every AI feature works with any provider, or none. gitai is an independent implementation of the publicly described design. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic. --- ## Why Classic Git hosting was built for humans who clone a repository, work for hours and push once. Coding agents work differently: thousands of short-lived tasks, each touching a few files, each wanting to land in seconds, all on the same branches. Full clones, merge queues and client-side history walks become the bottleneck. Scion's answer is to move the work to the server: clients stay online and fetch only what they need, history questions are answered (and cached) by the server, changes land through a compare-and-swap instead of a queue, every update is an entry in a changeset log, and the repository state lives in a consistent database plus object storage so servers scale out. gitai implements these ideas, with normal Git repositories underneath. ## The Scion ideas, implemented | Scion idea | In gitai | |---|---| | **Always-online clients** that fetch exactly what they need | `ObjectService` serves single objects and sparse trees; `graft clone` and `graft sparse` materialize only the paths you ask for. | | **Source control as an API**: history runs on the server | Blame, path history, ancestry and code search run server-side and are memoized as derived data, computed once per commit. | | **Landing without a merge queue** | `UserLand` rebases a change onto the current tip and lands it with a compare-and-swap; concurrent lands on one branch are batched into a single reference update. | | **Automatic conflict resolution** | A conflicting land is resolved by a resolver you choose (any LLM provider, a deterministic tool, or none) through a versioned, vendor-neutral protocol. | | **Changeset log** | Every accepted reference update is recorded with its operation and actor in a dense, ordered log that clients list or watch live. | | **Storage core: a database and object storage, stateless servers** | Each change is a changeset in a write-ahead log in SQLite or PostgreSQL, with a compare-and-swap per reference; packs live in object storage (file, S3, GCS, Azure). Server nodes are caches that any node can rebuild, so you add nodes to scale. | | **Test after landing, revert the culprit** | `graft-verify` tests the tip, bisects a failure and reverts the change that broke it. | | **Monitoring agents ("superfans")** | Agents follow the changeset stream and report what matters to each component, also through Slack. | | **Agent-friendly review** | Reviews with semantic approval rules: a comment-only change can need fewer approvals than a logic change. | | **Agents as first-class users** | Per-agent tokens, an RPC allowlist and branch policies decide what each agent may do. | | **Strict cache tiers** | `graft-cache` caches immutable objects in daemon and regional tiers, verifying every object. | ## Architecture ``` agents, CI jobs, sparse workspaces graft CLI / Go SDK | v gRPC +-------------------------------------------------+ | graft-cache (optional daemon and cache tiers) | +------------------------+------------------------+ v +---------------------------------------------------------------+ | gitai server (any number of nodes) | | land - objects - changesets - derived data - search - review | | write path: changeset + compare-and-swap per reference | +-----------+--------------------------------+------------------+ | | v v +-----------------------+ +-----------------------------+ | SQLite / PostgreSQL | | object storage | | changeset WAL, refs, | | content-addressed packs | | changelog, reviews | | (file, S3, GCS, Azure) | +-----------------------+ +-----------------------------+ \ / local Git repositories = caches any node can rebuild ``` Details: [ARCHITECTURE.md](doc/graft/ARCHITECTURE.md) and [STORAGE.md](doc/graft/STORAGE.md). ## Quick start Requirements: Linux or macOS, Go 1.26, a C toolchain, Meson and Ninja (the build compiles a bundled Git). ```shell git clone https://github.com/feder-cr/git-ai.git cd git-ai make build # server, CLI and tools into _build/bin examples/graft/quickstart.sh # a server, a cache daemon, two agents and a land, in a temporary directory ./_build/bin/graft # the CLI and its commands ``` To run your own server, adapt [`examples/graft/config.toml`](examples/graft/config.toml) and start it with `_build/bin/gitaly serve config.toml`. To put the repository state in a database and object storage, add a `[graft.storage]` section: start in `shadow` mode, import your repositories, then switch to `authoritative` ([STORAGE.md](doc/graft/STORAGE.md)). Inside the code the extensions are called **Graft**: the `[graft]` configuration section, the `graft` CLI, `internal/graft` and `doc/graft`. ## Documentation - [Quickstart](doc/graft/QUICKSTART.md) and [configuration reference](doc/graft/CONFIGURATION.md) - [Architecture](doc/graft/ARCHITECTURE.md) and the [storage core](doc/graft/STORAGE.md) - [Landing and batching](doc/graft/LAND-BATCHING.md), [conflict resolution](doc/graft/RESOLVE.md), [derived data](doc/graft/DERIVED.md) - [Review](doc/graft/REVIEW.md), [search](doc/graft/SEARCH.md), [verification](doc/graft/VERIFY.md), [superfans](doc/graft/SUPERFAN.md) and [Slack chat](doc/graft/SUPERFAN-CHAT.md) - [Agent security](doc/graft/AGENT-SECURITY.md), [benchmarks](doc/graft/BENCH.md), [fuzzing](doc/graft/FUZZING.md) - [Limitations and roadmap](doc/graft/LIMITATIONS.md) - Design documents of each phase: [PLAN.md](doc/graft/PLAN.md) to [PLAN6.md](doc/graft/PLAN6.md), and [PLAN8.md](doc/graft/PLAN8.md) (faster landing) ## Benchmark 50 agents land 5 changes each on one branch; 20% of the changes conflict on purpose. "Classic" is the same server with batching off: every agent rebases and retries its own compare-and-swap, up to 20 attempts. Measured with [`acceptance-phase4.sh`](examples/graft/demo/acceptance-phase4.sh) on one 16-core machine, two runs: | 50 agents, 250 changes | classic | gitai | |---|---|---| | changes landed | 100-101 | 200 | | attempts per landed change | 27 | 1.0 | | lands per minute | 240-272 | 1,862-2,544 | | p99 latency | 6.3-7.0 s | 1.5-1.8 s | The 50 changes gitai does not land are the planned conflicts: these runs use no conflict resolver. With the deterministic resolver of [`resolve.toml`](examples/graft/demo/resolve.toml) every conflict is resolved and all 250 changes land. Details and more sizes in [BENCH.md](doc/graft/BENCH.md). ## Status Version 0.2.0. Everything above is implemented and covered by unit, end-to-end, multi-node, crash and fuzz tests. Interfaces may still change before 1.0. Known gaps (for example garbage collection of packs in the storage core) are listed in [LIMITATIONS.md](doc/graft/LIMITATIONS.md). ## Community gitai is meant to be maintained by its community. Open an issue to report a bug or propose an idea, start a discussion before a large design change, and send pull requests: tests and a short description of the reasoning make them easy to review. The design documents in `doc/graft/PLAN*.md` explain why things are the way they are. ## Credits and license gitai is MIT licensed, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). It started as a fork of [Gitaly](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitaly), GitLab's Git RPC server (MIT, Copyright GitLab Inc.), which provides the Git plumbing underneath; every upstream Gitaly RPC keeps working. The non-MIT `ee/` directory of upstream Gitaly is not part of this repository. Gitaly's own README is kept in [doc/UPSTREAM-GITALY.md](doc/upstream/README-GITALY.md), and third-party notices are in [NOTICE](NOTICE).

items.readme:
# tv-vibehack **Your TV, minus the ads.** Strip the bloatware from any Android TV or Google TV over Wi-Fi, and replace the ad-filled home screen with a clean launcher that looks like an Apple TV. No root, no cable, nothing uninstalled, and a one-line restore if you change your mind. ![Before: stock Google TV home with a sponsored ad. After: the tv-vibehack launcher](docs/stock-vs-new-side.jpg) It started as an afternoon fixing my parents' Mi TV, which showed them an advert before they could reach Netflix. The whole thing was done with Claude Code talking to the real TV, and the prompt that did it is in this repo so you can do the same with yours. --- ## Table of contents - [How it works](#how-it-works) - [Quick start](#quick-start) - [What you get](#what-you-get) - [Supported TVs](#supported-tvs) - [Doing it by hand](#doing-it-by-hand) - [The launcher](#the-launcher) - [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) - [Questions people ask](#questions-people-ask) - [Contributing](#contributing) - [Licence](#licence) --- ## How it works Android TVs have the same debug bridge as Android phones. Once you switch on USB debugging in the TV's developer options, the TV listens on your Wi-Fi and asks you once to allow your computer. After that, everything is standard Android tooling: 1. **Back up** the list of installed packages and settings. 2. **Disable** the manufacturer's telemetry, ad services, content rows and preloaded junk with `pm disable-user`. Nothing is uninstalled, so a restore script can undo every step. 3. **Install** a small native launcher and make it the default home screen. The bloat differs by brand, which is why the prompt asks your coding assistant to discover it on your TV and ask you before touching anything you might use. ## Quick start You need a computer on the same Wi-Fi as the TV and a coding assistant with shell access (Claude Code, or anything similar). **1. On the TV** Settings → Device Preferences → About → press OK on **Build** seven times → go back → Developer options → turn on **USB debugging**. Some TVs also show a Network or ADB debugging toggle; turn it on too. Keep the TV switched on. **2. On your computer** Open your assistant, paste the prompt from [`PROMPT.md`](PROMPT.md), and fill in your TV model. **3. Follow along** Accept the "Allow USB debugging?" prompt when it appears on the TV, then answer the checklist questions: which streaming apps you use, which four go in the dock, whether to keep the voice assistant, Chromecast and firmware updates. That's it. The assistant backs up, debloats, builds and installs the launcher, and checks every step with screenshots pulled from the TV. On a 1 GB Mi TV the whole thing took one afternoon the first time; with this repo as context, people report about fifteen minutes. ## What you get A home screen that is yours again: - **Pitch-black background** and a dock of your four favourite apps at the bottom, in a lighter rounded band, exactly where Apple TV puts it. - **A top shelf** showing the focused app's name in large type, with an ambient glow in a colour taken from the app's own artwork. - **The rest of your apps in a grid** that slides up when you press Down. - **One floating glass highlight** that springs from tile to tile instead of each tile drawing its own border. The focused tile lifts slightly and shows its name. - **Three frosted buttons**: Inputs (a dropdown of HDMI ports, AV and Live TV), Wi-Fi (showing the network you're on) and Settings. - **A greeting, a large thin clock and the date**, set in [Outfit](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Outfit). - **A matching Clock screensaver**, optional, that drifts around the screen so nothing burns in. And a TV that stops working against you: no sponsored rows, no "Discover" nags, no analytics phoning home, no apps you never asked for. ## Supported TVs Anything running **Android TV** or **Google TV**: Xiaomi and Redmi, TCL, Hisense, Sony, OnePlus, Realme, Nvidia Shield and most others. Not supported: Samsung (Tizen), LG (webOS) and Amazon Fire TV. They run different systems or won't let a third-party launcher take over Home. Lists that people have tested and contributed live in [`examples/`](examples/): | TV | OS | |---|---| | Xiaomi Mi TV 4A (MiTV-MOOQ1) | Android TV 10 | | Xiaomi MiTV-AXSO0 | Android TV 9 | | TCL 55" 4K Google TV, 2023 (G10) | Google TV 12 | | SANYO ATV R2 | Android TV 9 | | OnePlus TV (D00) | Google TV 14 | Your TV not here? The prompt works regardless, it discovers the bloat itself. If you add your list afterwards, the next person with your model skips that step. See [Contributing](#contributing). ## Doing it by hand Everything the assistant does, you can run yourself. The tools need Python 3 and nothing else. ```bash python3 -m venv tools/venv && tools/venv/bin/pip install -r tools/requirements.txt export TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 # your TV's IP address tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/tv.py --probe # model, Android version, firmware tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/tv.py 'pm list packages' # run one shell command on the TV printf 'cmd1\ncmd2\n' | tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/tv.py --batch # several, one connection tools/disable.sh examples/xiaomi-mi-tv-4a/debloat.txt # apply a debloat list tools/restore.sh examples/xiaomi-mi-tv-4a/debloat.txt # undo it and restore the stock launcher ``` | Tool | What it does | |---|---| | [`tools/tv.py`](tools/tv.py) | A pure-Python ADB client: shell, batch, push, pull. Works where the stock `adb` binary is blocked. | | [`tools/b64push.py`](tools/b64push.py) | Uploads larger files such as APKs as base64 chunks and verifies the checksum. | | [`tools/disable.sh`](tools/disable.sh) / [`tools/restore.sh`](tools/restore.sh) | Apply or undo a debloat list. PowerShell versions sit next to them. | ### Windows The PowerShell scripts work without WSL or Git Bash. With Android Studio installed nothing else is needed: the install script uses Android Studio's bundled JDK and the default SDK location. ```powershell python -m venv tools\venv; tools\venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r tools\requirements.txt powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File launcher\build-and-install.ps1 -TvHost 192.168.1.50 powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\disable.ps1 -TvHost 192.168.1.50 examples\xiaomi-mi-tv-4a\debloat.txt powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\restore.ps1 -TvHost 192.168.1.50 examples\xiaomi-mi-tv-4a\debloat.txt ``` The install script stops before touching the stock launcher if the install or the home-screen switch fails. Git Bash also works; the `.sh` scripts detect a Windows venv and disable MSYS path rewriting themselves. ## The launcher A small native Android TV app (`com.gathin.tvhome`, about 1.6 MB), written in plain Java with AndroidX RecyclerView and nothing heavier. It is built for sets with 1 GB of RAM: no blur, no video, no network, no background services. **Configure** it in [`launcher/app/src/main/res/values/config.xml`](launcher/app/src/main/res/values/config.xml): the dock order, apps to hide, your TV's Live TV package, and the number of columns. **Build and install** with one command: ```bash TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 launcher/build-and-install.sh ``` It needs JDK 17 and the Android SDK (platform 34, build-tools 34.0.0). On macOS: ```bash brew install openjdk@17 android-commandlinetools sdkmanager "platforms;android-34" "build-tools;34.0.0" ``` Without Homebrew, the script also finds a JDK 17 known to `/usr/libexec/java_home` and an SDK in `~/Library/Android/sdk`, Android Studio's default. A release build (`./gradlew assembleRelease`) is smaller and faster on 1 GB sets; sign it yourself before installing. **Navigation** is deliberate: Up and Down move exactly one row, Up from the dock goes to the top buttons, the ends of the button row don't fall through to tiles, and the last focused app is remembered when you come back, even after the app list changes.
Optional: the Clock screensaver A large thin clock and the date over an ambient glow, in the launcher's style. Every minute the clock drifts to a new spot and the glow shifts colour. The system runs it only while the TV is idle. Turn it on over ADB, or pick "Clock" in the TV's screensaver settings: ```bash tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/tv.py 'settings put secure screensaver_components com.gathin.tvhome/.ClockDream; settings put secure screensaver_enabled 1' ``` It starts after the TV's "screen off" idle time (`settings get system screen_off_timeout`).
## Troubleshooting Things that bit us or contributors, so they don't bite you. **Connecting** - **macOS: `adb connect` says "No route to host"** although the port is open. Recent macOS treats the Google-signed `adb` as its own app under Local Network privacy and silently blocks it. `tools/tv.py` avoids the binary entirely. - **No "wireless debugging" toggle** on some TVs, Xiaomi among them. USB debugging alone opens network ADB on port 5555. - **Windows PowerShell 5.1 adds a byte-order mark** to text piped into a program, which turned the first batch command into gibberish. `tv.py` now strips it, and the `.ps1` scripts pipe clean UTF-8. - **Git Bash rewrites paths** like `/data/local/tmp` into Windows paths. The scripts set `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` for you. Set `JAVA_HOME` and `ANDROID_HOME` before building there. **Working on the TV** - **Chained `pm` commands** (`pm disable a; pm disable b`) may silently stop after the first. Run one per shell call; `--batch` does exactly that. - **Large pushes hang** through the Python client. Use `tools/b64push.py` for APKs. - **Screenshots come out empty** while Live TV or an HDMI input is on screen, seen on TCL. Press Home before `screencap`. - **Disable the stock launcher only after the new one is installed**, or the Home button lands on a factory test app. - **No on-screen keyboard** after switching launchers, seen on Xiaomi: the default input method pointed at a Baidu keyboard that isn't installed. Fix: `tools/tv.py 'ime set com.google.android.inputmethod.latin/com.android.inputmethod.latin.LatinIME'` - **Third-party launchers** often charge for basics like a custom wallpaper. That's why this repo has its own. ## Questions people ask **Is this safe? Can it brick the TV?** No. Nothing is flashed, rooted or deleted. Packages are disabled for the user profile, which lives in the data partition, not in the system image. The firmware is untouched. If something goes wrong, `tools/restore.sh` puts everything back, and even without the tools you can re-enable apps from the TV's own settings. **What about firmware updates?** Most lists disable the manufacturer's update service, so updates only arrive when you re-enable it on purpose. If an update does land, the worst case is that a package comes back enabled and you re-run the script. **Won't the apps break as their APIs change?** The streaming apps still update through the Play Store, which is left alone. The launcher doesn't talk to them; it lists what's installed and launches it, using Android launcher intents that have been stable for over a decade. **How did it get access? Isn't that a security hole?** Through the Android Debug Bridge, with one explicit "allow this computer" tap on the TV, the same as developing an Android app. The TV only trusts the key you approved. You can switch USB debugging off again afterwards and the launcher keeps working. **Can I just download the launcher APK?** Build it yourself with the one-line script above; it takes about a minute and you control what goes on your TV. We don't publish prebuilt binaries. ## Contributing The most useful contribution is your TV's debloat list, so the next person with that model doesn't have to rediscover it. Launcher improvements and sharper prompt wording are welcome too. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the format and the testing we ask for. ## Licence MIT, see [`LICENSE`](LICENSE). The Outfit typeface is under the SIL Open Font License, see `launcher/FONT-LICENSE-OFL.txt`.

items.title: ahwootech/BRUTAL
items.description: A free, open source C# framework for making games, or your own game engine. Direct access to native APIs and Vulkan, with the low-level libraries around them. The foundation under Kitten Space Agency and RimWorld's Waylith engine.
items.readme: # BRUTAL Framework **A free, open source C# framework for making games, or your own game engine.** BRUTAL is a framework. You can make a game directly with it, or use it as the foundation for a separate engine. We made Kitten Space Agency directly on BRUTAL. Ludeon built their Waylith engine on it to move RimWorld off Unity. At its core is a custom interop layer giving C# direct access to native APIs and libraries. Around that we've built mathematics, memory management, strings, collections, job scheduling, logging, localization, and bindings for Vulkan, GLFW, Dear ImGui, FMOD, RakNet, Jolt and Box2D. BRUTAL doesn't make the architectural decisions for you. You write your own stack. You can use whatever NuGet packages you want, including third-party ones. It's called BRUTAL for a reason. In some ways it's much harder to use than Unity, Unreal or Godot. In other ways, particularly if you're doing something unusual, it's considerably easier. You actually have to know what you want to do first. ## Why You are only as independent as your tools are. Developers have surrendered an extraordinary amount of control over their work to companies whose interests are not necessarily aligned with their own. We're not suggesting everyone should make their own game engine. We're suggesting every developer should have the option to, without having to spend four years building the foundations first. What that means in practice: - **Free, including for commercial games.** No royalties. We don't want a percentage of your game's revenue. We ask for credit. - **Open source.** The source is here under an MIT-based licence. If one day we stop being accountable to developers, you can fork it and go your own way. - **Deliberately small.** We do a few low-level things well: interop, memory, concurrency, maths, strings, and bindings to native libraries, on the latest C# and Vulkan. We avoid allocations and unnecessary overhead and use unmanaged memory and unsafe code where it makes sense. - **A foundation, like a kernel.** Think of the Linux kernel and something like Ubuntu. It's not an exact comparison, but it gets the idea across. We provide the foundation and you build your own systems on top. ### What BRUTAL is not BRUTAL is not trying to be a general-purpose engine. There is no editor, no scene graph and no renderer, and we're not adding them. We push back on efforts to add more, because adding everything is how the industry ended up with the kind of engines we don't want to use. Pull requests that drift away from a clear purpose will be rejected. ## Projects using BRUTAL | Product | Studio | Engine (if any) | | --- | --- | --- | | [RimWorld](https://store.steampowered.com/app/294100/RimWorld/) | Ludeon Studios | Waylith | | [Kitten Space Agency](https://ahwoo.com/app/100000/kitten-space-agency/) | RocketWerkz | Direct on BRUTAL | | Torpedia | RocketWerkz | Direct on BRUTAL | | Art of the Rail | RocketWerkz | Direct on BRUTAL | | [Gruntz](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ROB5IilenZE) | RocketWerkz | Direct on BRUTAL | | Afterskies | Floating Origin Interactive | Direct on BRUTAL | Ludeon report 2 to 4 times the performance of the Unity build in their own tests, with the vast majority of existing mods still compatible. See their [Steam announcement](https://steamcommunity.com/games/294100/announcements/detail/672882362547178634). Kitten Space Agency is a free pre-alpha spaceflight simulation. It runs a solar system at real scale, and is the first major project built directly on BRUTAL. [Download it on Ahwoo](https://ahwoo.com/app/100000/kitten-space-agency/) and see the technology yourself. ## What is in the box Each top-level folder in this repository is one library, published as a NuGet package. Reference only the ones you need. | Library | What it is | | --- | --- | | `Brutal.Core` | Base types, attributes, platform detection, pointer helpers, Roslyn analyzers | | `Brutal.Interop` | The custom interop layer that gives C# direct access to native APIs | | `Brutal.Memory` | Unmanaged memory management and allocators | | `Brutal.Collections` | Collections that don't allocate | | `Brutal.Strings` | String building and handling without allocation | | `Brutal.Maths`, `Brutal.Numerics` | Vector, matrix and numeric types | | `Brutal.Concurrency` | Job system and threading | | `Brutal.Logging` | Logging | | `Brutal.Localization` | Localization | | `Brutal.Vulkan`, `Brutal.Vulkan.Abstractions`, `Brutal.Vulkan.Vma` | Vulkan bindings, abstractions and the Vulkan Memory Allocator | | `Brutal.OpenGl` | OpenGL bindings | | `Brutal.ShaderC`, `Brutal.Slang` | Shader compilation | | `Brutal.Glfw`, `Brutal.Sdl`, `Brutal.Sdl.Image`, `Brutal.Sdl.Mixer`, `Brutal.Sdl.Ttf` | Windowing and input, with SDL's image, audio mixing and font add-ons | | `Brutal.ImGui`, `Brutal.ImGui.*`, `Brutal.ImPlot` | Dear ImGui and ImPlot bindings, docking branch | | `Brutal.Render.Mesh` | Mesh utilities | | `Brutal.Texture`, `Brutal.Texture.Abstractions`, `Brutal.Ktx`, `Brutal.Gli`, `Brutal.Stb` | Texture loading, KTX and compressed formats, image decoding | | `Brutal.Gltf`, `Brutal.MeshOptimizer` | glTF loading and mesh optimisation | | `Brutal.FreeType` | Font rasterisation | | `Brutal.Fmod`, `Brutal.OpenAl` | Audio | | `Brutal.RakNet` | Networking | | `Brutal.Jolt`, `Brutal.Box2D` | 3D and 2D physics | | `Brutal.Monitor.Common`, `Brutal.Monitor.Host`, `Brutal.RenderDoc`, `Brutal.RenderDoc.ImGui` | Runtime monitoring and RenderDoc capture integration | | `Brutal.NativeFileDialog`, `Brutal.NotCurses`, `Brutal.ZLib` | Native file dialogs, terminal UI, compression | Third-party notices for each library live in its `LICENSES` folder, `Brutal.ImGui/LICENSES` say. ## Getting started ### Prerequisites - [.NET 10 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download) - A Vulkan 1.3 capable GPU with current drivers (if you render) - The [Vulkan SDK](https://vulkan.lunarg.com/) if you want validation layers while developing - Windows or Linux ### Your first window Create a project and add Core and Glfw: ```sh dotnet new console -n HelloBrutal cd HelloBrutal dotnet add package Ahwoo.Brutal.Core dotnet add package Ahwoo.Brutal.Glfw ``` Replace `Program.cs`: ```csharp using Brutal.GlfwApi; using Brutal.Numerics; if (!Glfw.Init()) throw new Exception("Failed to initialize GLFW"); Glfw.WindowHint(GlfwWindowHint.ClientApi, 0); var window = Glfw.CreateWindow(new GlfwWindow.CreateInfo { Title = "Hello BRUTAL", Size = new int2(1280, 720), }); while (!window.ShouldClose) Glfw.PollEvents(); Glfw.Terminate(); ``` ```sh dotnet run ``` That opens a window with no graphics API. What you add next is up to you: - **Rendering:** `Ahwoo.Brutal.Vulkan.Abstractions` and `Ahwoo.Brutal.Vulkan.Vma` for a Vulkan renderer, `Ahwoo.Brutal.ShaderC` to compile shaders at runtime. - **Debug UI:** `Ahwoo.Brutal.ImGui` and `Ahwoo.Brutal.ImPlot`. - **Parallelism:** `Ahwoo.Brutal.Concurrency` for the job system. - **Audio and networking:** `Ahwoo.Brutal.Fmod`, `Ahwoo.Brutal.RakNet`. Questions and "how do I" threads go on the [Guides and Help forum](https://forums.ahwoo.com/forums/brutal/guides-and-help/). ### Building from source This is the source for every published package. Project files, a solution and build scripts are coming. Until then use the NuGet packages, and use this repository to read and fork the code. ```sh git clone https://github.com/ahwootech/BRUTAL.git ``` ## Licence BRUTAL is free to use, modify and distribute, including in commercial games. There are no royalties and we don't want a percentage of your game's revenue. The licence is based on MIT with an added attribution requirement. A game or product built with BRUTAL: 1. includes the BRUTAL copyright notice in its credits screen, or equivalent (section 2.1) 2. shows the BRUTAL logo before gameplay starts (section 2.2) 3. ships `NOTICE.txt` alongside the product (section 2.3) If you don't want to do that, we can arrange a separate commercial licence. We also waive the logo requirement for non-profit projects and where displaying it would be detrimental to the application's purpose. BRUTAL is open source. There are already OSI-approved licences that allow graphical attribution. Ours is not yet OSI approved because we have not submitted it yet. We intend to, and to develop the licence with community feedback. See [LICENSE.txt](LICENSE.txt) for the full text. Third-party components keep their own licences. Section 4.0 points at the `LICENSES` folder at the root of each NuGet package; in this repository, those notices are in the `LICENSES` folder of each library that redistributes them. ## Contributing You can submit PRs and issues. We are a small team and maintaining a public framework is going to be a lot of work, so please be patient with us. We'll see what happens, assess the problems, and change our workflows as necessary. What won't change is BRUTAL's scope. Before opening a PR, read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). It covers scope, what we expect from AI-assisted contributions, the contribution grant in section 5.0 of the licence, and the sign-off every commit needs. Small changes you understand and have tested, with a clear purpose, are the ones that will get merged. - Security issues: report them privately, see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). Don't open a public issue. - Conduct: [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). ## Community - Source: https://github.com/ahwootech/BRUTAL - NuGet packages: https://www.nuget.org/profiles/Ahwoo - Forums: https://forums.ahwoo.com/forums/brutal/ - Discord: https://discord.gg/MEuNTYbAh8 ## Credits BRUTAL was made by the RocketWerkz Enterprise team and others, named in [CONTRIBUTORS.md](CONTRIBUTORS.md). When we talk about wanting credit for BRUTAL, these are the people we are talking about. BRUTAL is Copyright (c) 2024 Ahwoo Limited.

items.title: chenglou/handwired
items.description: Turn your regular JavaScript code into a neural net.
items.readme:
# Handwired

Turn your regular JavaScript code into a neural net; no training, exact, yet also fully differentiable!

## How It Works

A program's made of if-else, loops, and state. Handwired transforms them into matrix multiplication + reglu over floats. For example:

```ts
const a = 5
const result = (a > 4) ? 10 : 12
```

The above can be expressed as basic arithmetic:

```ts
const a = 5
// Math.max(0, x) is ReLU. For an integer a, above4 is 1 if a > 4, and 0 otherwise
const above4 = Math.max(0, a - 4) - Math.max(0, a - 5)
// Both branches compute, and above4 picks one
const result = above4 * 10 + (1 - above4) * 12
```

You can calculate that by hand and see that both arrive at the same result.

We then collect the + and * and relu into a giant matmul, and either run it on JS or WebGPU, for fun.

Because we basically only use these 2 primitives:
- the full program stays differentiable
- the weights don't need training since they're written manually
- existing gpu techniques, such as fusion, sparsity, reordering, have a great time optimizing such minimal primitives

This unlocks lots of funny use-cases, like:
- unfreezing the weights and train them (what does that even do? Let's find out!)
- attaching a specific frozen program to a generic neural net and train end-to-end (now a nanoGPT can do both Shakespeare and your particular UI?)
- achieving GPU-level of parallelism with JS code that was written in a traditional single-threaded way (see the JSON search demo that runs in milliseconds over 100k documents)

## Play With It

Try the demos live: https://chenglou.me/handwired/

`git clone && bun install`, then `bun start` to run them locally. Check `docs/`, `src/` and `template/` to get started! (`lab/` is a bunch of old experiments you can check or ignore)

items.readme:
# Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection for Windows

**Uncharted 1, 2 and 3 from the PS4 collection running natively on Windows 10 and 11, by [SuperMedo](https://github.com/Supermedo).** Mohammed Albarghouthi

Same idea as my [Bloodborne port](https://github.com/Supermedo/bloodborne_pc): the original PS4 game
code runs directly on your PC and the graphics are translated to Vulkan. Unpack the zip, start
`Uncharted.exe`, pick your game folder, choose a game and press **PLAY**.

**[Download the latest version](https://github.com/Supermedo/uncharted_pc/releases/latest)** · **[Join the Discord](https://discord.gg/s3RgH6cRfJ)**

> **No game files are included.** You need your own decrypted dump of the collection
> (CUSA02343, CUSA02320, ...: the folder with eboot.bin, big2-ps4_Shipping.elf,
> big3-ps4_Shipping.elf, sce_sys, u1data, u2data and u3data).
> This project is not affiliated with Sony Interactive Entertainment or Naughty Dog.

## Features

- All three games from one launcher: Drake's Fortune, Among Thieves and Drake's Deception.
- 60 FPS like on PS4, or 120 FPS (higher rates are experimental).
- Anti-aliasing with TAA, AMD FSR 3.1, AMD FSR 4 or NVIDIA DLSS (DLAA).
- Frame generation: AMD FSR 3 (any GPU) or NVIDIA DLSS (RTX 40 2x, RTX 50 up to 4x).
- Keyboard, mouse and controller together, all remappable. Mouse look in U3.
- Add to Steam and desktop shortcuts from the launcher, automatic updates.

## Requirements

- Windows 10 (1903 or later) or Windows 11, 64-bit.
- An Intel Core 4th generation (Haswell) or newer, an AMD Ryzen, or an AMD FX.
- A graphics card with Vulkan 1.3 and a current driver, with **6 GB of video memory or more**.
  4 GB cards (GTX 1650, RX 570) run out of video memory and crash after a while; on those, keep
  Anti-aliasing and Frame generation off.
- About 8 GB of free memory (RAM + page file).

## Known problems

- **Uncharted 3, Cartagena square (chapter 2):** at high frame rates (240 Hz setting, ~80 FPS)
  the game could freeze and close with "GPU crash: the graphics device was lost". It came from
  the speed fix for that area and is fixed in 0.3. If it still happens to you, set Frame rate to
  60 on the Display page and open an issue with your `user\last_run.log`.
- **Uncharted 3:** green or black shapes flash for a single frame on some characters (Sully's
  shirt in Cartagena). It happens in shadPS4 too, so it's a shader translation problem. Not fixed yet.
- **Crash with "ASSERTION: GetRenderFrameParams(frameToFreeInstancesFor)->m_gfxEopTick"**
  (mostly U1 after the first cutscene): the game expected the GPU side to be done with a frame it
  wanted to reuse, and stopped when it wasn't yet (shaders building on a first run). Fixed in
  0.3.2 (0.3.4 for the 1.02 versions): the game now waits for it. If you still see it, open an
  issue with your log.
- **Intel HD / UHD graphics:** a black screen on the HD 630 is fixed in 0.3.3. Older Intel chips
  (HD 520) can still crash inside Intel's own driver.
- **Uncharted 3 London bar crash** (fault at `0xd9c59b`, or device lost in the bar fight): fixed in
  0.3.4.
- **Uncharted 2 loading crashes** (`ReadSync file (req/read: ...)`, white textures then
  `iSubMesh < m_numSubMeshInstances`): file reads could come back cut short. Fixed in 0.3.5.
- **Older CPUs:** the games use instructions of the PS4's processor (AVX, BMI1, MOVBE, LZCNT).
  AMD FX runs since 0.3.6 (its missing MOVBE is emulated, a bit slower). Intel Core 3rd generation
  and older can't run the games yet; the game says so instead of crashing with 0xc000001d.
- **Uncharted 2, train wreck:** `IsFinite(deltaTransform)` in character-leg-ik.cpp, fixed in 0.3.6
  for the EU 1.00 version.
- Frame rates above 120 are experimental.

## Building

MSYS2 CLANG64 on Windows: `bash build.sh` builds `out\bb-probe.exe`, and
`bash packaging/windows/package.sh` makes `dist\uncharted-windows` and the zip.

## Credits

Built on [bbport](https://github.com/deadinside28/bloodborne_pc), the native Linux port of
Bloodborne by deadinside28, and on the [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4)
renderer. Video decoding (Videodec2) and the DLSS bridge come from
[IFreemz/shadPS4-Bloodborne-DLSS-FSR](https://github.com/IFreemz/shadPS4-Bloodborne-DLSS-FSR).
Thanks to Mindro for the shadPS4 Uncharted build that showed which problems to look for.

Also used: [FSR-Vulkan](https://github.com/FireBurn/FSR-Vulkan) and the AMD FidelityFX SDK (FSR),

var(--cds-scroll-fade-bottom) * .3), #0000000d calc(100% - var(--cds-scroll-fade-bottom) * .15), transparent ); ``` ### 2. 麦克风 8% 底噪门限截断与原生 Web Audio 振荡器无损合成 (Noise Floor Gating & Synthetic SFX) * **痛点**：语音会话模式中空调等环境底噪容易导致波形持续微震抽搐；同时传统 Web 音效加载外部 MP3 有网络延迟并伴随切断爆音。 * **Claude 算法**：一是引入 8% 噪声门限过滤（`NOISE_FLOOR = 0.08`）物理截断底噪；二是基于原生 Web Audio `OscillatorNode` 进行纯代码频率调制（如 440Hz → 880Hz 上扬）与平滑指数淡入淡出（`exponentialRampToValueAtTime`），零外部音频依赖且彻底消除爆音。 ### 3. CJK 输入法合成双重互锁守卫 (IME Composition Guard) * **痛点**：中日韩用户在拼音/假名输入法候选词浮层敲击 Enter 键确认汉字时，消息被粗暴误发送。 * **Claude 算法**：构建 `!(e.nativeEvent.isComposing || e.keyCode === 229)` 双重互锁守卫，并在按键拦截状态机中接管 `Escape` 键，防止候选词关闭时意外冒泡退避整个对话窗口。 ### 4. 150ms 冷却时间戳防抢夺视口图钉 (Scroll Pinning Cooldown) * **痛点**：流式 Token 生成时，用户向上滚动查阅历史消息，会被源源不断的生成内容强制拉回底部。 * **Claude 算法**：建立 40px 底部容差图钉锁定 + 150ms 人工滚动冷却时间戳机制。用户一旦主动向上微移视口，系统立即锁定滚动权限 150ms，彻底杜绝“自动滚动抢夺屏幕”。 ### 5. 以鼠标光标为物理不动点的仿射 Pan/Zoom 方程 * **痛点**：普通画廊放大图片时以视口中心为原点，导致鼠标想查看的细节区域被推离屏幕。 * **Claude 算法**：将光标指针 $(O_x, O_y)$ 视为物理世界不变不动点，解算仿射变换矩阵： $$\text{idealTx} = O_x - (O_x - \text{prevTx}) \cdot \frac{S_{\text{target}}}{S_{\text{current}}}$$ 配合 4px 手部微抖死区与视口边界溢出阻尼系数 ($y = 0.7$)。 ### 6. 麦克风 6 频段非线性 Gamma 幂律能量压缩 * **痛点**：直接将分贝映射为波形高度会导致低音爆格、说话停顿时空调噪音引起持续微抖。 * **Claude 算法**：引入 8% 噪声门限过滤底噪，叠加 0.7 次幂非线性 Gamma 压缩： $$\text{Compressed} = \min\left(1, (\max(0, E - 0.08) / 0.92)^{0.7} \times 1.5 \times W_b\right)$$ 使微弱的人声细语被温和放大，高分贝爆音被自然平抑，波形动态范围极其均匀。 ### 7. Shadow DOM 隔离 + CSS Grid 行高几何硬锁 * **痛点**：代码差异对比引擎在遇到长行换行（Word Wrap）时，左侧行号与右侧代码经常严重错位。 * **Claude 算法**：采用 Shadow DOM 隔离语法选择器，左右两栏在 CSS Grid 中被强制同步硬锁为相同网格行跨度：`gridRow = span ${lines}`，并使用 `feed: e.slice(m.length)` 增量向 Worker 发送 Delta，避免 $O(N^2)$ 重复语法树重排。 ### 8. Iframe 事件防吞噬护盾与双击 50/50 吸附 * **痛点**：拖拽 Artifacts 双栏分割条划过内部展示 iframe 时，iframe 截获指针事件导致拖拽状态死锁卡住。 * **Claude 算法**：拖拽激活瞬间向全局注入 `data-pane-dragging="true"`，在预览容器上方强制覆盖一层透明的 `pointer-events: none` 阻断层；双击手柄瞬时触发二阶弹簧 50/50 平分居中吸附。 --- ## 📂 项目结构 (Repository Structure) ``` open-claude-ui/ ├── assets/ # 资产说明与合规指引 │ ├── images/logo.svg # 开源矢量标识 │ └── README.md # 资产合规与系统级回退栈说明 ├── code-examples/ # 30 个生产级独立代码文件 (开箱即用) │ ├── ArtifactsSplitPaneResizer.tsx # 双栏弹性分割与折叠引擎 │ ├── AttachmentCard.tsx # 附件磁贴与上下文胶囊 │ ├── cds-theme.css # 全局主题样式表 (CSS 自定义属性与 Keyframes) │ ├── CdsButton.tsx # 4 级尺寸、5 大变体全能按钮 │ ├── ChatComposer.tsx # 核心输入框终端 │ ├── ChatMessageBubbles.tsx # 会话气泡套件 (User & Assistant) │ ├── ClaudeAudioPlayer.ts # 低延迟音频引擎 (内置 Web Audio 原生合成振荡器) │ ├── ClaudeDesktopHeader.tsx # macOS 沉浸式标题栏组件 │ ├── ClaudeMotionPresets.ts # 动效引擎与二阶阻尼谐振子数学求解 │ ├── CodeBlock.tsx # 代码块容器与 2.5s 复制衰减状态机 │ ├── ConfirmationDialog.tsx # 模态确认对话框 │ ├── ContainerResponsiveBar.tsx # 自适应容器查询响应栏 │ ├── CoworkAgentCanvas.tsx # 多智能体协同看板与拓扑空间 │ ├── createClaudeMainWindow.ts # Electron 宿主主窗口创建工厂 │ ├── DraggableSessionList.tsx # 侧边栏会话拖放与固定物理 │ ├── EpitaxyIframeBridge.tsx # Artifacts 预览沙箱桥接器 │ ├── LiveMicActivityBars.tsx # 6 频段非线性麦克风波形柱 │ ├── McpToolDecisionCard.tsx # MCP 交互式工具调用决策卡片 │ ├── MediaLightboxViewer.tsx # 多模态媒体查看器与画廊跑道 │ ├── ModelSwitcherWithTokenGauge.tsx # 模型矩阵选择器与 Token 仪表盘 │ ├── ReasoningAmbientGlow.tsx # 动态光效与推理氛围感组件 │ ├── RichComposerWithMentions.tsx # CJK 守卫、/ 与 @ 双触发符输入终端 │ ├── ScrollFadeContainer.tsx # 7 档非线性 Alpha 渐变遮罩 │ ├── SegmentedControl.tsx # 999px 全圆角分段选择胶囊 │ ├── StatusIndicators.tsx # 陶土呼吸灯、运行脉冲与骨架屏扫光 │ ├── StreamingDiffViewer.tsx # 代码差异对比与流式高亮引擎 │ ├── tailwind.config.js # Tailwind 配置工程扩展 │ ├── ThinkingAccordion.tsx # 思考过程状态机折叠组件 │ ├── useClaudeRovingFocus.ts # 全键盘无障碍焦点漫游 Hook │ ├── useClaudeScrollPinning.ts # 流式滚动视口图钉 Hook │ ├── useClaudeSharedElementTransition.ts # View Transitions 共享元素变形 Hook │ └── useRateLimitBackoff.ts # 429/503 指数退避与熔断状态机 Hook ├── docs/ │ ├── Claude Design System (CDS).md # 七大篇章 / 31 小节深度技术指导手册 │ └── claude-components-storybook.html # 交互式可视化故事书 (双击即可离线体验) ├── src/ │ └── index.ts # 统一对外导出的 TypeScript 库入口 ├── package.json ├── tsconfig.json └── README.md ``` --- ## items.readme:
Quickstart  ·  Examples  ·  Models  ·  Cloud  ·  Docs

# Tell it the task. It opens a browser and gets it done. Scout is an open-source agent that uses a real browser to finish a task for you. Describe what you need in plain words. Scout reads the page, clicks, types and scrolls until the job is done, then hands back the answer. If it cannot finish, it tells you what is missing and returns what it found. **Scout runs best on Outcrawl's cloud.** One line gives it a browser that sites treat like anyone at home, with captcha solving and a replay of every run. It also runs on your own machine.

A recorded run on Outcrawl's cloud, 13 October 2026, shown at 6x speed with nothing cut.

## Start in three steps **1. Install Scout.** You need Node 22 or later. On the cloud there is no browser to install. ```sh npm i @outcrawl/scout ``` **2. Add your keys.** An Outcrawl key for the browser ([get one free at outcrawl.ai](https://outcrawl.ai): 1,000 credits every month, no card needed) and a key for your model. Scout works with any AI model service that speaks the standard chat completions API, including a model running on your own computer: ```sh export OUTCRAWL_API_KEY=your-outcrawl-key export SCOUT_BASE_URL=https://your-endpoint/v1 export SCOUT_API_KEY=your-model-key export SCOUT_HANDS_MODEL=your-model-id ``` **3. Give it a task.** Save this as `task.ts` and run `npx tsx task.ts`: ```ts import { Scout } from '@outcrawl/scout'; const scout = new Scout({ browser: 'outcrawl', models: { hands: { model: process.env.SCOUT_HANDS_MODEL!, baseURL: process.env.SCOUT_BASE_URL!, apiKey: process.env.SCOUT_API_KEY!, }, }, }); const result = await scout.run('Find the top three stories on Hacker News right now'); console.log(result.data); console.log(result.replayUrl); // watch the whole run, step by step ``` Scout opens a browser on Outcrawl's cloud, works through the page, and prints the answer with a link to the replay. **Rather use a browser on your own machine?** Install one with `npm i playwright-core && npx playwright install chromium`, then change the one line to `browser: { launch: {} }`. Add `headless: false` inside `launch` to watch it work. Replays come with the cloud, so `replayUrl` stays empty on your own browser. > [!TIP] > Not writing the code yourself? Give this page to your coding agent and ask it to set Scout up and run your task. ## What you can ask it to do Tasks you would do in a browser yourself, written the way you would ask a colleague. Each of these is a working example you can run: - **Research.** "Go to Hacker News and report the three stories with the most comments: title, link and comment count." [`research.ts`](packages/scout/examples/research.ts) - **Fill in a form.** "Order a pizza on this form, then tell me exactly what the shop received." [`form-fill.ts`](packages/scout/examples/form-fill.ts) - **Compare.** "Find these two books and compare their price and stock, then tell me which is cheaper." [`compare.ts`](packages/scout/examples/compare.ts) - **Sign in.** "Sign in with these details and read the welcome message." [`login.ts`](packages/scout/examples/login.ts) - **On the cloud.** The research task on Outcrawl's cloud, with a link to watch the replay. [`outcrawl.ts`](packages/scout/examples/outcrawl.ts) Want the answer in a fixed shape, such as a list of names and prices? Pass a JSON Schema with the task and the answer comes back in exactly that shape. ## Bring your own models Scout has no built-in model and no default. You choose a model for each job, on any service that speaks the chat completions API: a hosted provider, a gateway, or a server on your own machine. Each job can use a different model and a different key. | Job | Needed | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | | `hands` | Yes | Reads the page and takes each step: click, type, scroll, read. It runs on every step, so a fast model pays off here. | | `brain` | No | Plans the run and decides each step. Helps long tasks that cross many pages. | | `eyes` | No | Looks at a screenshot when the page has to be seen. Needs a model that accepts images. | | `extract` | No | Reads a page into your answer or your schema. Without it, `hands` does this. | ```ts models: { hands: { model: 'your-fast-model', baseURL: urlA, apiKey: keyA }, brain: { model: 'your-strong-model', baseURL: urlB, apiKey: keyB }, eyes: { model: 'your-vision-model', baseURL: urlA, apiKey: keyA }, extract: { model: 'your-local-model', baseURL: localUrl, apiKey: '' }, } ``` If a service refuses Scout's request for a structured reply, the run's error says which job it was and what to change: set `structuredOutput` on that job to `'json_object'` or `'strict'`. ## The best way to run it: Outcrawl's cloud

Many sites stop a browser that runs from a data center or behaves like a script, and a task that stops halfway is no answer at all. On Outcrawl's cloud, Scout gets a browser built to get through: - **Residential connections.** Traffic leaves through ordinary home connections, so sites load the way they do for anyone at home. - **Captcha solving.** Challenges are answered inside the browser, and the run carries on. - **Natural input.** The browser plans every pointer move, scroll and keystroke itself, so Scout sends it plain actions. - **Recordings.** Runs are recorded by default, and `result.replayUrl` opens a step-by-step replay. - **Nothing to install.** No browser to download, update or keep running on your machine. **Measured:** runs on Outcrawl's cloud reached **92.5%** of pages on Browser Use's 80-site benchmark, scored with their own code; the next best reached 81.4%. Three full runs, 7 October 2026. [Method and every run](https://outcrawl.ai/resources/benchmarks). A cloud run is billed as an ordinary Outcrawl browser session, and your model calls still go to your own services. Every account gets 1,000 free credits a month, no card needed. [Get a key at outcrawl.ai](https://outcrawl.ai). ### Other browsers Scout drives any Chrome or Chromium, so moving between them is one line; your models and your task stay the same. ```ts // On Outcrawl's cloud (recommended) browser: 'outcrawl' // On your machine, started for you browser: { launch: {} } // A browser you already run, over CDP browser: { cdpUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:9222' } ``` ## What you get back Every run returns a result, even one that falls short: - `status`: `completed`, `partial`, `capped` (a limit you set was reached) or `failed`; - `data`: the answer, in your schema's shape when you passed one; - `error`: on a partial or failed run, what is still missing; - `steps`: every action taken, with its timing and whether it worked; - `costUsd`: the run's model spend, when it is known; - `replayUrl`: on Outcrawl's cloud, a link to watch the run. Limit a run with `caps: { steps, duration, budget }`. Reaching a limit is a normal ending, with everything found so far. The full API is in the [package reference](packages/scout/README.md). ## Inside this repository | Package | What it is | | --- | --- | | [`packages/scout`](packages/scout) | The front door: `new Scout({ browser, models }).run(task)`. | | [`packages/runtime`](packages/runtime) | The agent loop: look at the page, pick an action, act, check, repeat. | | [`packages/model`](packages/model) | The model side of the loop: prompts, the job split, structured replies, provider-neutral clients. | | [`packages/scout-core`](packages/scout-core) | Shared types and helpers. | | [`packages/scout-cdp`](packages/scout-cdp) | Drives a real browser over the DevTools protocol: navigation, clicks, typing, scrolling, tabs, snapshots. | | [`packages/agenthands`](packages/agenthands) | Pointer and keyboard input planning for local browsers (MIT, its own licence). | To work on Scout itself: ```sh bun install cd packages/runtime && bun test ./test ``` ## Contributing Pull requests are welcome: bug reports, fixes and new examples alike. Sign off each commit (`git commit -s`, the [Developer Certificate of Origin](https://developercertificate.org/)). This repository is an automatic mirror. Every change lands first in the repository Outcrawl runs in production, ships with its tests, and then arrives here in a sync commit, so a merged pull request comes back to you as part of the next sync. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) has the details. ## Licence Apache-2.0, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). `packages/agenthands` keeps its MIT licence. Copyright 2026 Aeonmind LLC.


Scout is made by Outcrawl, web infrastructure for AI agents.

# GPTibo

**可自托管的数字商品商城，包含用户前台、管理后台与代理工作台。**

[![CI](https://github.com/CoolkHz/gptibo/actions/workflows/verify.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/CoolkHz/gptibo/actions/workflows/verify.yml)
[MIT License](LICENSE) · [快速开始](#快速开始) · [后端文档](services/storefront/README.md) · [安全说明](SECURITY.md)

GPTibo 将商品展示、下单支付、订单交付、售后处理和代理商店管理整合在同一套系统中。前端使用 React 与 TypeScript，后端提供 Go + PostgreSQL 和 Cloudflare Workers + D1 两种实现，便于按部署环境选择和二次开发。

原站点已停止运营，项目现以 MIT 许可证开放源码。支付与供应商接入使用匿名适配器，需要配置自己的服务后使用。

## 功能

| 模块 | 能力 |
| --- | --- |
| 用户商城 | 商品与套餐展示、下单、支付状态、订单查询、售后申请、中英文界面、深浅色主题 |
| 管理后台 | 商品定价、订单与客户管理、退款处理、代理管理、结算与通知配置 |
| 代理工作台 | 独立商店、品牌设置、自定义域名、商品管理、订单统计与下级代理管理 |
| 业务后端 | 身份验证、支付回调、采购适配、异步任务、邮件通知与交易状态管理 |
| 开发与部署 | 数据库迁移、Docker Compose、自动化测试、GitHub Actions 与源码安全扫描 |

## 技术栈

| 层级 | 技术 |
| --- | --- |
| 前端 | React 19、TypeScript、Vite、Tailwind CSS |
| Go 后端 | Go、Gin、PostgreSQL，API 与业务 Worker 分进程运行 |
| Cloudflare 后端 | Workers、D1、Wrangler |
| 邮件 | React Email |
| 验证 | Node.js Test Runner、Go Test、Gitleaks |

两套后端均服务于商城。当前公开版本包含商城侧供应商适配器，**不包含独立供货平台及供应商执行系统**。

## 快速开始

### 环境准备

- Node.js 24、npm、Git、Python 3。
- 使用 Go 后端时，准备 Docker Compose；原生开发需要 Go 1.26+ 和 PostgreSQL。
- 使用 Cloudflare 后端时，通过项目内的 Wrangler 运行本地环境。

```sh
git clone https://github.com/CoolkHz/gptibo.git
cd gptibo
npm ci
```

选择下面一种后端方式运行。

### 方式一：Go + PostgreSQL

在仓库根目录执行以下命令，初始化本地秘密、数据库和运行角色：

```sh
cd services/storefront
python3 scripts/init-secrets.py
cp .env.example .env
docker compose config --quiet
docker compose build api
docker compose up -d --wait postgres
docker compose --profile maintenance run --rm maintenance migrate
docker compose --profile maintenance run --rm maintenance grant-runtime
docker compose up -d --wait api worker
```

另开终端，在仓库根目录启动前端：

```sh
npx vite --config services/storefront/vite.config.ts
```

访问 `http://127.0.0.1:5175`。前端会将 `/api` 请求代理到本机 Go API 的 `8093` 端口。

原生启动、管理员登录、邮件服务与接入配置见 [Go 后端文档](services/storefront/README.md)。Windows 用户可使用后端目录中的 `scripts/init-secrets.ps1` 初始化秘密。

### 方式二：Cloudflare Workers + D1

在仓库根目录执行：

```sh
cp .dev.vars.example .dev.vars
npx wrangler d1 migrations apply gptibo-local --local
npm run preview:worker
```

默认访问 `http://127.0.0.1:8787`。需要前端热更新时，另开终端运行 `npm run dev`，访问 `http://127.0.0.1:5173`；API 请求会转发到本地 Worker。

`.dev.vars` 保存本地配置，不应提交。远程部署时需创建自己的 Cloudflare 资源，并替换 `wrangler.jsonc` 中的占位配置。

### 页面入口

| 页面 | 路径 |
| --- | --- |
| 商城 | `/` |
| 管理后台 | `/admin` |
| 代理工作台 | `/partner` |

管理员登录需要配置自己的管理员身份、TOTP 和邮件验证服务。默认配置不提供可直接登录的管理员账号，也不会发起真实支付、采购或通知。

## 项目结构

```text
src/                   商城前台、管理后台与代理工作台
services/storefront/   Go API、业务 Worker、迁移与部署配置
worker/                Cloudflare Workers 后端
migrations/            D1 数据库迁移
emails/                邮件模板
tests/                 前端与 Worker 业务测试
scripts/               构建与源码检查脚本
public/                静态资源
.github/workflows/     持续集成
```

## 配置与接入

| 配置文件 | 用途 |
| --- | --- |
| [services/storefront/.env.example](services/storefront/.env.example) | Go 后端基础运行配置 |
| [services/storefront/.env.integrations.example](services/storefront/.env.integrations.example) | Go 后端支付、采购及通知接入 |
| [.dev.vars.example](.dev.vars.example) | Cloudflare 本地配置 |
| [wrangler.jsonc](wrangler.jsonc) | Worker 与 D1 资源配置 |

供应商适配器使用 `recharge`、`account_supplier`、`delivery_supplier`、`xgift` 等通用名称；`gatewaya`、`gatewayb` 为匿名聚合支付适配器。请依据自己的服务协议核对地址、签名、商品映射、金额和回调，再开启对应功能。

真实商户身份、密钥、账号凭据和生产数据不随源码提供。`example.invalid` 是不可用于真实接入的保留域名，示例商品与金额仅用于演示。请使用新数据库安装；匿名化后的迁移不兼容原生产数据库。

## 开发与验证

在仓库根目录执行：

```sh
npm test                # 前端与 Worker 业务测试
npm run lint            # 静态检查
npm run build           # 类型检查、邮件模板与前端构建
npm run security:scan   # 公开源码检查
```

Go 后端验证：

```sh
cd services/storefront
go test ./...
go vet ./...
```

完整数据库测试需设置 `STOREFRONT_TEST_DATABASE_URL`，连接本机、库名以 `_test` 结尾的专用数据库；未配置时集成测试会跳过。详细要求见[后端测试说明](services/storefront/README.md#测试)。

自动化测试不连接真实支付或供应商服务。生产部署前，需要在自己的环境验证完整交易流程。

## 参与贡献

欢迎通过 [Issues](https://github.com/CoolkHz/gptibo/issues) 反馈问题或提出建议，也欢迎提交 Pull Request。

1. 描述问题、预期行为和复现步骤。
2. 提交范围明确的改动，涉及交易或账务逻辑时补充回归测试。
3. 运行与改动相关的检查，在 PR 中说明验证结果。

请勿提交真实凭据、用户资料、生产日志或数据库。安全问题请按 [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) 中的方式报告。

## 许可证

项目代码采用 [MIT License](LICENSE)，允许在保留版权与许可声明的前提下使用、修改和分发。

第三方资源遵循各自许可证，商标及美术作品权利归原权利人所有。详见[品牌资源说明](public/brands/README.md)与[第三方样式说明](src/styles/vendor/README.md)。
